text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- Extension of NATO into eastern Europe would pose a danger, warns international Pugwash peace committee, saying Hungary and Czech Republic in NATO would revive old hostility between Russia and the west.

- There is a hidden wisdom in old people's apparent loss of touch with reality and living in the past, says American therapist Noami Feil. They usually try to recollect past painful experiences, or seek clarification of past things left undone.
- Finnish blacksmiths obliged to import foreign expertise because the craft has disappeared from among Finns.
- The fall in stainless steel prices has finally come to a halt. In Europe, prices have risen 10 percent within in the last week and North America is expected follow.

- Kone says its business acquisition from the U.S. a few years back have fulfilled all the expectations and operations are profitable. "The only problem is that the growth of elevator markets has stopped," Kone spokesman says.
- From next year it will be possible to purchase goods from the Internet by credit card.
- A 73-year old Finnish woman was robbed in New York while suffering a heart attack on the street.
- The Estonian police department is trying to lower the number of car crashes that police are involved in. Finnish police have been called to give driving lessons.
- Two Finnish men set a new record on Saturday by sitting for 300 hours in a car.
